correctness.rationale: Uniform drift contraction at rate at least a−g constructs the unique stationary process from the infinite Brownian past, with finite moments. Reflecting Y and the shared telegraph sign gives zero cross-product at every time pair; simultaneous inversion of X and Y gives both zero means (the reflection alone would only give the Y mean). As a separate reconstruction, condition on the sign path: the law is centered Gaussian, with equal diagonal covariance S and off-diagonal L satisfying S′=−2aS+2gσL+2D and L′=−2aL+2gσS. These yield E[S]=D(a+q)/(b+aq) and close the linear stationary system for E[S²], E[σSL], E[L²], including the −2q multiplier for sign-bearing moments. Solving gives κ₄=3 Var(S)=3D²g⁴q/[a(b+aq)²(2b+aq)], independently matching the frozen position-generator solution. Normalizing yields the stated excess. The derivative sign numerators for the two scaled profiles are 1−x−x² and r−rt−t². They change sign exactly once on the positive axis. The raw peak value follows by φ²=φ+1; at t=r/φ the excess root polynomial is r(r−1)<0. The roots scale as r/φ and √r in units of a, giving the stated separation.
residual_risks: The optimization holds at fixed a,D,g using q as the flip rate in each direction, not the telegraph correlation-decay rate 2q. No claim for independent switches on the two couplings or for auto-correlations.
